title: fix(core,app-shell,plugin-detail): freeze the write census's backlog; the record feed and a related list's Add existing / fallback remove read the affordance-to-grant map (objectui#12082)
body:
Part of #12082 (the census freeze and leg B's non-Setup sites; the four Setup entries stay on the card)
Clause-②: yes

Claim `6108058067` (seat `domain:ui#2`), triage `6102063887`. Implemented by an `os-dev` run dispatched from session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01TYgwmFK1q4KJ6Qq2WRLzsD`.

`Clause-②` is `yes`, not the claim's predicted `no`: four rows join `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS`, a published value of `@object-ui/core`, so core is `minor`. The contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed.

## What lands, in triage's order

### 1. The backlog freeze, and leg A's `HOST_GATED` limit closed

- `UNMAPPED_BACKLOG` (the census pin `affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx`) is a closed list of the keys `WRITE_SITES` may grade `unmapped`, held equal to the ledger both ways. A NEW `unmapped` entry is red until graded; a key graded out of `unmapped` must leave the list. It was frozen at the 13 keys on BASE, and each later commit deletes the keys it grades. At this head it holds the four Setup assignment keys only.
- The hand-written `HOST_GATED` list is replaced by a derivation, `hostGatedSites`: a mapped site is host-gated when a file it names in `readBy` JSX-mounts the component the write is written in, and then every mount must be in `readBy`. Measured on this tree it finds exactly the site the list held (the import wizard). So a NEW host-gated component needs no list entry to be seen. What it cannot see is written beside it: a host that reaches the write through a hook, a function, an alias or a wrapper component, not a JSX element of the component's own name.

### 2. Leg B: the nine non-Setup sites, reach measured per site

| Site | Reading | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| record feed: `handleAddComment`, `handleAddReply` (create `sys_comment`) | reachable: the composer is drawn for every caller, and the `everyone` baseline grants no `sys_comment` bit (an app grants it). Read on objectstack `main` `67b669e6`: `member_default` names no `sys_comment`; `viewer_readonly` has `'*'` read with no create; the showcase app's sets name `sys_comment` zero times; the security middleware's step "2. CRUD permission check" maps insert to `allowCreate` and refuses with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | **mapped** to a new row `feedComment` (create) |
| record feed: `handleToggleReaction > write` create / delete (`sys_comment_reaction`) | reachable: the same reading; the reaction object's own docblock and its floor pin say its create / read / delete bits come from an app-shipped set, never the baseline | **mapped** to new rows `feedReactionAdd` (create) and `feedReactionRemove` (delete) |
| record feed: `handleToggleReaction` update (`sys_comment` column store) | reachable on a deployment with no `sys_comment_reaction` | **mapped** to a new row `feedReactionColumn` (update) |
| dashboard designer: `saveSchema` (update `sys_dashboard`) | the target does not exist: `sys_dashboard` is a per-type table objectui retired (dashboards persist through `/meta`, ADR-0034, the header of `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts`), and objectstack `main` registers no such object (absent from the spec's `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` and `CLOUD_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES`; the repo tree has no dashboard object file, control `sys-comment-reaction.object.ts` 1 hit). The Save fails for every caller whatever the grant, and no in-app link reaches `design/dashboard/NAME` | **outOfFamily**, with that reading |
| related list: `handleAddRecords` create (`linkField` set) | reachable: the Add button showed for every caller. Measured where the write goes: a link row of the list's OWN object (the junction) | **mapped** to `relatedNew` (reused: create on the list's object) |
| related list: `handleAddRecords` update (no `linkField`) | measured: re-parents the PICKED record (`add.picker.object`) | **mapped** to `relatedRowEdit` (reused: update on that object) |
| `record:related_list`: the fallback remove | reachable, and worse than "reads no grant": on a record page the host bridge withholds `onDelete` exactly when `relatedRowDelete` is closed, and the fallback (an `add` config, no host delete) then put the delete straight back | **mapped** to `relatedRowDelete` (reused), read with the list object's registered schema, so it never re-opens what the host closed |

H4's two candidates were both right, one per branch: the junction branch is `relatedNew` on the junction, the re-parent branch `relatedRowEdit` on the picked object.

### The record feed, how it reads the rows

`RecordDetailView` hands each handler to the discussion context only where its row allows it, and the panel draws the composer, the reply input and the reaction picker from the handler's presence. Each row is asked of the object it writes, with that object's schema from the registry, so policy and the effective operation set are read too. On the records store the control is the add row; a take-back click asks the remove row and, closed, writes nothing (no write the server would refuse, and nothing shown changed). With no permission provider every grant reads open, as before.

## Evidence

- **Measured on BASE first** (`c9fc10b1`, restore-trapped): the four source files checked out at BASE (4/4 blobs equal BASE on disk, each fix anchor `grep -c` 0), the HEAD pins and census run against them: `Test Files 4 failed (4)`, `Tests 20 failed | 64 passed (84)`. Red per pin, every red in the defect direction (an affordance offered under a grant that does not hold it): feed 9 of 18, Add existing 5 of 9, fallback remove 4 of 8, census 2 of 49 (the row table and the mapped-site check). Controls stayed green (no provider; the full shape; the host's own delete). Restore: 4/4 blobs equal HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, status clean.
- **Ablations**, objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` WRAP mode, predictions written first, each restore `blob == HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` empty:
  - A1 grade an existing mapped entry `unmapped`: census 1 failed / 48 passed, the freeze test (`added`). As predicted.
  - A2 put a graded key back into `UNMAPPED_BACKLOG`: census 1 failed / 48 passed, the freeze test (`left`). As predicted.
  - A3 plant a JSX mount of `ImportWizard` in a file that reads no `listImport`: census 1 failed / 48 passed, the host-gated mount test. As predicted.
  - A4 hand `onAddComment` over unconditionally: feed pin 4 failed / 14 passed (the four closed composer shapes); the census stays green, since the file still reads `feedComment`. As predicted: the runtime pin catches what the census cannot.
  - A5 the junction Add reads `relatedRowEdit`: 3 failed (census: no file it names reads `relatedNew`; Add pin: the create-only and edit-only junction shapes). As predicted.
- **Suites and gates**: the readings at the final head are in the `os-dev-report` comment on the card. At open: pins + census green on the main merge (`84 passed`); all 48 `RecordDetailView*` files `312 passed`; `plugin-detail` shard 1/4 `713 passed | 8 skipped`; `type-check` of `core`, `plugin-detail`, `plugin-form` exit 0, each echoing its own script, 0 `error TS`; eslint on the 8 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` 0 errors, and each modified source file's warning count equal to BASE.

## Acceptance notes

- **The reply composer cannot be reached from a read row.** `RecordActivityTimeline` draws `ThreadedReplies` (and the reply input) only when `replyCount` is above 0, and nothing derives `replyCount` on read: the record page sets it only after a reply is posted in the session. `sys_comment`'s own docblock says the count is taken from `parent_id` children at read time. So a reply read back from the server is not shown, and the reply input appears on no read row. The reply site is still mapped to `feedComment` (same row and gate as the composer). Noted, not filed: no reach measured at a door.
- **A partial reaction grant.** A caller who can create but not delete their reaction row gets the control, and a take-back click writes nothing. A caller who can delete but not create gets no control, so cannot take back an older reaction. Both follow from one control that both adds and takes back.
- **The dashboard designer's Save is a dead write.** Graded `outOfFamily` with the reading above. The route has no in-app entry (the dashboard view's top-bar "Design in Studio" deep-links to Studio's own surface), so it is reached by URL or the recent list only, and a Save there fails silently (`saveSchema` swallows the error). Noted, not filed.
- **Object verdict only**, as on leg A: no per-record author check (the server's own comment gate also asks author-or-parent-editor of an update, and the column store's reaction update is one).
- The feed reads `sys_comment` / `sys_comment_reaction` schemas from the page's `objects`; absent, the default bucket is read, so the grant and the operation set still decide.
